newsitem.title: UK: Bass says talk it dropped C-T "speculation".
newsitem.headline: Bass says talk it dropped C-T "speculation".

text.p: Brewer and hotels group Bass Plc said talk that the company had abandoned its planned acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley was just speculation.
A spokesman for Bass said: "This is speculation. We have had no indication from the MMC about their thinking."
Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission handed over its findings on the proposed acquisition to trade secretary Ian Lang today.
Many analysts believe the conditions imposed by the MMC are too onerous to make the deal workable for Bass, specifically because it requires Bass to sell off its 1,400-strong pub lease company.
Bass shares were off 7-1/2p at 854p in early trade.
"I've been told it's not going through, Bass is not prepared to give up the estate," said one analyst who chose not to be named.
The 1,400 pubs are strong performers compared to the industry average. In terms of beer sales, they take some five to seven barrels a week against about four elsewhere.
The division turned in trading profits of 61 million stg last year, giving profit of some 42,000 stg per pub.
"The Bass leased estate has always been one of the most profitable in the industry and it is not something they will give up with ease," said another analyst who declined to be named.
Although market speculation about the MMC terms was rife, analysts said the company is unlikely to have seen the MMC's findings itself and will wait to hear from the authorities before deciding.
Under the terms of the deal analysts view Bass as a winner whether the deal is allowed to go through or not.
If the ruling goes against it, Bass could sell on Allied Domecq's stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Carlsberg for 110 million stg and Allied will repay Bass 30 million.
In that event the whole saga will have cost Bass 60 million which will to some extent be offset by the fact Bass is entitled to 50 percent of C-T's profits since the deal was first announced.
Bass agreed to take control of C-T last August and paid Allied 200 million stg for its half share in C-T.
Danish brewer Carlsberg agreed to contribute its half share in C-T plus 20 million in return for a 20 percent interest in the merged company.
